episodes.body:

Kurtis Kallenbach has spent years researching one deceptively simple question: what actually happened at the moment of your birth, biologically and legally, and what did you unknowingly give up?

His answer runs through embryology, maritime admiralty law, biblical allegory, and etymology. The zygote is your complete biological estate — every chromosome, encoded in one cell, bounded by the pelucid membrane like a property fence. The umbilical cord cut creates a legal severance between you and that origin. The birthday document registers the event in a maritime system that treats your body as cargo delivered to a berth. The amnion — the lamb of god — becomes a bounty. And knowing none of this is precisely how the system maintains its hold.

Topics: fertilization as the only true origin of the species; why conception was legally redefined after Roe v. Wade and why the word matters; the zygote as a complete biological estate; the pelucid membrane as a natural property boundary; why the birthday is a legal device not a biological reality; the umbilical cord cut as the crafty severance creating maritime personhood; the bar association as the hyphen in Judeo-Christian — a bonding agent between two artificially separated states; Jesus as the amnion and the physician who says "they that are whole need not a physician"; why wholeness through knowledge is the only remedy; and what the word "jellyfish" actually reveals about the spineless legal fiction created by the cut.
